definition: Cleaned list price of a product.
transformation: None for EDA; log1p(price) for skewed models; scale later (train only).
analytical_purpose: Candidate cost signal for H3 at product level.
limitations: List price is not routine cost; currency and size not known; discounts missing.

definition: log(1 + price).
transformation: np.log1p on valid non-negative prices.
analytical_purpose: Reduces right skew so plots and distance-based methods are readable.
limitations: Zero and invalid prices need a stated rule; not interpretable in raw units.

definition: Price divided by product size (ml or g).
transformation: price / size after unit harmonising.
analytical_purpose: Fairer cost comparison between small and large products.
limitations: Size column may not exist or may use mixed units; otherwise stays a proposal.

definition: Draft step type from category: cleanser, toner, serum, moisturizer, sunscreen, mask, exfoliant, eye_care, other, unknown.
transformation: Keyword rules; review mapping table by hand.
analytical_purpose: Basis for step-type counts and category comparisons (indirect proxy for H1).
limitations: Rules are a draft and may misclassify real categories.

definition: One 0/1 column per step type.
transformation: One-hot encoding (handle_unknown='ignore').
analytical_purpose: Lets models and groupby tables use step type.
limitations: Many 'other' items can hide real differences.

definition: Number of distinct ingredients in the cleaned list.
transformation: Integer; NA when the list is missing (not 0).
analytical_purpose: Rough formulation complexity; related to H4 only indirectly.
limitations: Missing is not zero; lists can be incomplete or ordered differently by source.

definition: 0/1 flags for ingredient groups such as fragrance, drying alcohols, retinoids, exfoliating acids.
transformation: Match whole ingredient names against a dictionary taken from a cited source.
analytical_purpose: Exploring whether product compatibility concerns cluster in some formulations (H4).
limitations: A flag is not proof of irritation. The dictionary needs a reliable source and name variants.

definition: 1 if the ingredient list is missing.
transformation: status == 'missing'
analytical_purpose: Keeps missingness visible; may be informative about source quality.
limitations: May reflect data source rather than product.

definition: Existing *_missing_flag and *_invalid_flag columns, plus a per-row count of flags.
transformation: Sum of flag columns per row (n_quality_flags).
analytical_purpose: Checks whether data quality varies by segment; sensitivity analysis.
limitations: Row count of flags mixes different problems; keep individual flags too.

definition: Mean review rating per product.
transformation: groupby mean; compute inside training data only when used in a model.
analytical_purpose: Product-level satisfaction signal (H5).
limitations: Few reviews give unstable means; also compare with product-table rating.

definition: Number of valid reviews per product.
transformation: Count; log1p.
analytical_purpose: Shows how reliable product-level averages are.
limitations: Popularity effect; not quality.

definition: Share of reviews with rating 1 or 2.
transformation: Mean of (rating <= 2) per product; report with n.
analytical_purpose: Simple product-level dissatisfaction signal (H5).
limitations: Threshold is a convention; needs minimum review count.

definition: Word and character count of cleaned text; very-short flag.
transformation: Already computed; log1p for skew.
analytical_purpose: Controls for text length in text analysis; data-quality check.
limitations: Length is not sentiment.

definition: 0/1 flags for review mentions of time, irritation or reaction, price, and difficulty of use.
transformation: Whole-word regex matches; negation handled in a second pass or by manual check.
analytical_purpose: Explores H2, H3, H4 and H5 through what reviewers write.
limitations: Words are proxies; sarcasm and negation cause errors; lists need manual validation on a labelled sample.

definition: Sentiment score of the review text.
transformation: Lexicon method such as VADER, or another method justified and checked on a small hand-labelled sample.
analytical_purpose: Text-derived satisfaction signal (H5).
limitations: Lexicons are built for general social media text; skincare words may be mis-scored. Needs validation first.
leakage_note: Medium: model must not see future text

definition: Skin type reported by the reviewer, with an 'unknown' level.
transformation: Standardised categories; one-hot encoding.
analytical_purpose: Segment comparisons (H4).
limitations: Self-reported and often missing; sensitive attributes are excluded elsewhere.

definition: 1 if the reviewer recommends the product.
transformation: Binary parsing (Week 3).
analytical_purpose: Satisfaction proxy (H5).
limitations: Not present in every source; a recommendation is not routine adherence.

definition: Number of distinct steps a person actually uses in their routine.
required_inputs: survey or diary: list of products or steps per person
transformation: Count of distinct steps (optionally by step type).
analytical_purpose: Direct test of H1 against verified dropout.
limitations: Cannot be built from public data.

definition: Estimated minutes per day spent on the routine.
required_inputs: survey or diary: minutes per step or total
transformation: Sum over steps; or step_count x median minutes per step with the assumption written down.
analytical_purpose: Direct test of H2.
limitations: Self-reported time is rough; any per-step assumption must be documented and checked.

definition: Cost of one use of a product, and monthly cost of the whole routine.
required_inputs: price, size, usage amount per use, uses per week (survey)
transformation: price / number of uses per container; sum over routine products per month.
analytical_purpose: Direct test of H3.
limitations: Needs usage amount; discounts and gifts distort cost. Assumptions must be stated.

definition: Interaction of step count and time burden.
transformation: Product of centred (and scaled) values, only after both main effects are in the model.
analytical_purpose: Checks whether many steps hurt more when each is slow.
limitations: Correlated with its parts; hard to interpret; needs enough data.

definition: Product-level share of reviews with irritation or reaction keywords.
transformation: Mean flag per product; report with n.
analytical_purpose: Public proxy for product compatibility (a candidate BRFS component).
limitations: Keyword proxy only; reviewers who stopped using the product may not post.

definition: Year (or month) of the review.
transformation: Extract year; treat as categorical or time index.
analytical_purpose: Checks time trends and drift in ratings.
limitations: Date format must be confirmed; many missing dates possible.
